title: Signal handoff snapshot — late June cadence
content:
Shift window: 2029-06-25 19:00 UTC -> 2029-06-26 03:00 UTC
Owner: Maya Chen (night primary) — handoff to Liam O'Connor (graveyard)

High-level summary:
- Quiet start, then two notable signal clusters around 20:40 and 01:05 UTC.
- User-visible impact limited to ~7% increased 5xxs on /v1/embeddings for 18m (20:40–20:58). Tail latency spikes for chat endpoints at 01:05 for ~11m while autoscaler oscillated.
- No full-service outages. No customer SLA breaches; accounted in PD incident notes.

Incident A — transient KV-cache eviction ripple (PD-INC-48291)
- Time window: 20:40–20:58 UTC.
- Symptoms: sudden uptick in 500s from embeddings route; request latency for first-token generation jumped from median 90ms to 300–700ms for a subset of requests.
- Trigger: correlated with a rolling background cleanup job that executed region-wide against the prefix cache on deduped nodes (cron: cache-prune-region). Rough hypothesis: tag mismatch caused broader prefix invalidation and many requests missed KV cache causing heavy decode kernel activations and GPU queueing.
- Immediate mitigation taken: paused cache-prune-region (ops-id: pause-2029-06-25-20:45) and promoted warm-cache fallback for embeddings (route policy set to soft-warm).
- Rollback/cleanup: cache-prune resumed after small patch to selector; we left prune window staggered by 30s per pool.
- Impact containment: throttled new heavy requests via temporary token-level quota reduce (config: quotas/temp-embeds-26jun).
- Follow-ups required:
  - Confirm root cause: run cache-prune simulation locally with dataset slice A (Diego to add synthetic load). JIRA: JIRA-INFRA-3172.
  - Add a kill-switch to the cleanup cron that respects a health-check endpoint to avoid global invalidations. (Owner: Priya)
  - Runbook delta: add step to verify per-pool cache-hit heatmap before pruning. (Owner: Maya)

Incident B — autoscaler flapping (eu-west)
- Time window: 01:05–01:16 UTC.
- Symptoms: sustained queue growth on dedicated pools serving chat-latency tier, repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles (~3 cycles) causing tail latency jitter.
- Trigger: noisy VM health probes from a recent instance image (kernel update) produced intermittent negative health reports; autoscaler treated that as capacity loss.
- Immediate mitigation: applied temporary static override to keep current instance count while we rolled back the suspicious instance image on eu-west pool (override id: fix-autoscale-0625).
- Result: queue drained and tail latency returned to baseline by 01:22 UTC.
- Follow-ups required:
  - Validate image health probe sensitivity matrix; add hysteresis to the scale decision (Owner: infra-team, Diego).
  - Add alert rule that triggers on >2 scale cycles within 10m to route immediately to on-call infra (so we don't rely on silent metrics).

Operational notes (things you should know at handoff)
- Current active PD incidents: PD-INC-48291 (embedding cache evictions) — marked acknowledged but stabilized. No action expected next shift unless Jira shows failing tests.
- Service flags toggled during shift: quotas/temp-embeds-26jun=ON, autoscale-override-eu-west=ON.
- Config locations:
  - quotas/temp-embeds-26jun -> Console > Configs > Temporary Quotas (link in PD ticket)
  - autoscale overrides -> infra-admin > scale-overrides (internal only)

Open follow-ups and ownership (short list)
- Maya: Draft runbook change for cache-prune behavior (add pre-check heatmap) — due EOD next Tue.
- Priya: Implement kill-switch on prune job (prototype by next shift).
- Diego: Reproduce cache invalidation locally, attach logs to JIRA-INFRA-3172; also validate image probe matrix for eu-west (blocker for infra change).
- Infra team (oncall rotation): Add hysteresis patch to autoscaler and deploy to staging, then canary to eu-west.

Quick wins to reduce noise
- Reduce prune job concurrency (we changed it already to be staggered); consider defaulting prune to per-pool windows.
- Increase debounce window on autoscaler health-decisions from 30s to 90s for critical pools.

Action items for next shift (priority order)
1) Monitor PD-INC-48291 for reoccurrence; if errors trend up, revert prune immediately and open critical incident bridge.
2) Validate that quotas/temp-embeds-26jun is rolled back once cache-hit returns to baseline.
3) Confirm progress on JIRA-INFRA-3172; if reproduction not attached by 09:00 UTC, escalate to Diego and tag in Slack #infra.
4) Review staging autoscaler hysteresis patch and coordinate canary window with infra lead.

Notes-to-self / rough thoughts
- We saw a small set of customer requests produce very high token counts after cache misses; might need to add request-level guardrails to avoid multi-second decode bursts.
- Consider an experimental local LRU sampler to estimate hit-rate before full prune.
- Documentation: add explicit note in runbook that cache-prune is a global-impact job and must have manual sign-off during peak windows.

Logs & attachments (quick references)
- PD incident timeline: appended to PD-INC-48291 (see linked_artifacts).
- Kibana queries used: "errors.query:/v1/embeddings AND status:500 AND region:us-west-2" and "queue.length > 50 and pool:chat-latency".
- Relevant PRs: internal patch to prune selector (PR-7891), autoscaler debounce experiment PR-7924 (staging only).

Handoff checklist (what I did while leaving)
- Saved heap/kv snapshots to s3://ops-dumps/night-2029-06-25/cache-prune-snap-1
- Notified product on incident via #prod-ops (message id: slack:CAT-2029-06-25-21:03)
- Created JIRA-INFRA-3172 and linked PD incident
- Toggled autoscale-override-eu-west=ON (leave for next shift to remove after canary)

Who to ping if stuff breaks
- Infra pager: Diego Ramos (oncall), backup: Priya Gupta.
- Serving runtime lead: @serving-runtime on Slack (channel: #serving-runtime).
- SRE escalation: @bridge-lead (for incident declaration).

Miscellaneous notes (informal)
- Customer X mentioned degradation in #cust-of-note — we replied with the short explanation and that we were investigating. Keep PRs/notes visible to CS for follow-up.
- I left some raw traces in ops-dumps for later triage — could be useful for reproducing decode spikes.

End of handoff — leaving a few TODOs in the JIRA and pinging next shift in Slack now.

-- Maya
